traditional.text: We have a law!

remedy.text: But the Jews wouldn't have this Roman insinuate that he was more just than they, so they shouted, "Our law says he deserves death, because he, a mere man, claims to be the Son of God!"

4.why: Jennings' level-four correlate is the Pharisees' cry: the codified rule settles the matter, and the rule-breaker, even a healer, must be punished.

traditional.text: I would not have known what sin was had it not been for the law. For I would not have known what coveting really was if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."

remedy.text: What shall we say then? Is the law evil and selfish because it increases the amount of evil and selfishness we see? Absolutely not! I would not have known what evil and selfishness looked like if it wasn't for the diagnostic efficacy of the law. I would not have realized that coveting was evil and selfish if the law didn't say, "Don't covet."

4.why: The written law as a diagnostic instrument that tells the sick they are sick; Jennings says God gave it because sin-damaged minds could no longer comprehend his law of love directly, and the detailed code was for those at level four and below.

traditional.text: We know that the law is good if one uses it properly. We also know that law is made NOT for the righteous, but for lawbreakers and rebels, the ungodly and sinful, the unholy and irreligious; for those who kill their fathers or mothers, for murderers, for adulterers and perverts, for slave traders and liars and perjurers—and for whatever else is contrary to the sound doctrine that conforms to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which he entrusted to me

remedy.text: We know that the written law is a diagnostic instrument for the soul, and it is good if used properly. We also know that this diagnostic tool was not made for the spiritually healthy, but for those who are selfish in character, those who are spiritually diseased, who don’t know God, who don’t love others but kill their fathers and mothers, the ill at heart, murderers, sexual perverts and adulterers, human traffickers, liars, deceivers, and for everyone and everything else that is out of harmony with God’s design for life or doesn't harmonize with the incredible truth about God's character of love that he has entrusted me to share.

4.why: Jennings quotes this to explain why God used law at all: it is made for the lawbreaker, not the righteous, a diagnostic tool, which fits his point that the detailed codes were given for those at level four and below.

traditional.text: Jesus reached out his hand and touched the man. "I am willing," he said. "Be clean!" Immediately he was cleansed of his leprosy.

remedy.text: Jesus gently reached out and touched the man whom no one else would touch, and said, "I am very willing. Be clean!" Immediately he was cured, the leprosy disappeared, and his skin became healthy and normal again.

5.why: Touching a leper broke the rules and healed a man; Jennings puts it first in his list of Jesus' level-five acts, where what helps the person decides what is right.
5.context: Jennings lists Jesus touching lepers as level-five functioning (GodShapedHeart.md line 374) but does not quote the verse; NIV text supplied, verify.

traditional.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.' This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments

remedy.text: Jesus confidently said, "'Love the Lord your God with your entire being, heart, soul, and mind.' This is the foundation upon which life exists and is therefore the first and greatest commandment. And the second is the natural product of the first: 'Love others as yourself.' All God's laws–design protocols–and the teachings of God's spokespersons are built upon these two commandments."

5.why: Jennings says that once a person matures to level five and above the whole law can be summed up in these two statements, and the detailed rules fall away.

traditional.text: Love does no harm to a neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law

remedy.text: Love is the principle of beneficence and does no harm, but does only what is in the best interest of another, therefore love is the law upon which life is based.

5.why: Level five defines wrong as objective harm to another and right as real benefit; Paul's one-line summary is that definition.

traditional.text: All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had.

remedy.text: All those who had partaken of the Remedy and trusted Jesus were united in love, sharing a common purpose. No one thought selfishly or claimed possessions for self, but with love for others shared everything they had.

6.why: Jennings' level-six correlate is the apostles after Pentecost living in harmony with God's design, loving God and others more than self, with no rule requiring it.
6.context: Jennings names the apostles after Pentecost as the level-six correlate (GodShapedHeart.md line 374) but does not quote Acts; NIV text supplied, verify.

traditional.text: This is the covenant I will establish with the people of Israel after that time, declares the Lord. I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people

remedy.text: This is the healing plan I will renew with the house of Israel after that time, declares the Lord: I will recreate and cleanse them, and restore my law of love in their minds, and write my principles of benevolence on their hearts. I will be the God they love, admire and adore, and they will be a people who reveal my true character.

6.why: The law written on the heart is Jennings' marker for the move past level four: the principle is now internal, so the external code is no longer needed to diagnose.

traditional.text: Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.

remedy.text: Do not continue to practice the destructive methods of selfishness, which infect the world, but be completely transformed into God's image by the renewing of your mind. Then you will value God's principles, practice his methods, and discern his will–his good, pleasing and perfect will.

6.why: Level six is a renewed mind that understands how life is built to work and chooses it intelligently; this is the text for a transformation that is cognitive before it is behavioral.
6.context: Page-chosen; not quoted by Jennings in the cited files.

traditional.text: I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master's business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you.

remedy.text: I do not want you to be my servants, because servants only do what they are told but do not understand what the master is doing, nor do they understand the master himself. Their hearts are not in harmony with the master, and what they do they do not do freely. I want you to be my friends — to understand what I am doing — and to freely choose to be in unity with me. That is why I have told you about everything the Father and I are working to accomplish, so your hearts and minds will be in harmony with us.

7.why: Jennings builds level seven on this verse: the friend, unlike the servant, knows the master's business and chooses to cooperate in his purposes.

traditional.text: those who do not love their lives so much as to shrink from death

remedy.text: They overcame him by partaking of the Remedy–the perfect character of Christ the Lamb, symbolized by his blood–and by the evidence of their self-sacrificing lives, as they no longer loved their own selves so much as to shrink from death: they were healed to love just like Jesus.

7.why: Jennings describes the sealed, translation-ready people of level seven with this phrase: love for God and his purposes outweighs even survival.

traditional.text: Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.

remedy.text: Now, eternal life is this: having an intimate knowledge of you, and connection with you — the only true God, and me — Jesus Christ, your Son whom you have sent.

7.why: Level seven is defined by understanding, by actually knowing God; Jennings cites this verse for the friends who know God personally and can therefore say of him what is right.
7.context: Jennings cites John 17:3 in the servants-and-friends post (line 27) and the roads post (part 1, line 33) but does not quote it; NIV text supplied, verify.

roads.frame_caveat: These eight walks are the blog's own frame for locating yourself on the journey of life. Jennings does not map them onto the seven levels of moral decision-making, and this page does not either; read them as a second, independent mirror, not as a key to the levels.

intro.text: But not all methods of travel are equally healthy, adaptable, or capable of getting us through those rough patches. As you travel the roads of life, consider which way you would like to navigate them:
intro.speaker: Jennings

walks.title: Walking in Ignorance

quote.text: Those who walk in ignorance are those who don’t know God and His methods of love. If you are walking in ignorance, I encourage you to get to know God, for this is the road to eternal life (John 17:3).
quote.speaker: Jennings

traditional.text: At that time you were apart from Christ. You were foreigners and did not belong to God’s chosen people. You had no part in the covenants, which were based on God’s promises to his people, and you lived in this world without hope and without God

remedy.text: That was before your minds were enlightened about Christ–and therefore you were separate from him–and you were not members of Israel (who was God’s spiritual health-care team), and therefore were unacquainted with God’s plan to heal and restore. Your condition was terminal, because you were without God — and therefore without hope — and in the darkness of the world.

scripture.why: The post uses Paul's description of life apart from Christ for those who do not yet know God or how life was built to work.

traditional.text: As obedient children, do not conform to the evil desires you had when you lived in ignorance. But just as he who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do; for it is written: “Be holy, because I am holy

remedy.text: As children who have thought through the issues and now understand God's principles and agree with his methods, no longer allow fear and selfish desires to control your actions as you did before you knew the truth about God. But just as God is pure, undefiled and holy, accept his healing and live pure, undefiled and holy lives; for God has said, "You will be pure and holy–just like me–for I am pure and holy."

scripture.why: The post's hope for the ignorant: the ignorance was a stage, and God calls people out of it.

walks.summary: Hurting people who have never known God or his design for life, and whose efforts at peace keep failing.
walks.self_check: When I try to fix my life, do I actually know how God designed it to work, or am I guessing?

walks.title: Walking in Illiteracy

quote.text: Those who walk in illiteracy claim a belief in God but don’t actually know what He’s doing. I encourage you to read about God’s hand in history and to no longer have a faith floundering in biblical illiteracy.
quote.speaker: Jennings

traditional.text: Now these things occurred as examples to keep us from setting our hearts on evil things as they did… These things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come

remedy.text: Since we suffer with the same sickness of heart and mind as they did, all of this history is recorded for our benefit–to warn and protect us–so we won't refuse the Remedy as they did, but will fulfill God's purpose of victorious living at this present time.

scripture.why: The post's reason the Bible's history matters: it was written down so that we would learn from it, and the illiterate believer cannot.
scripture.remedy_scope: Remedy text given for verse 11 only; the post quotes verses 6 and 11.

walks.summary: Church-going believers who say they believe in God but have essentially no knowledge of what Scripture records him doing.
walks.self_check: Could I tell the story of how God dealt with Moses, David or Manasseh without looking it up?

walks.title: Walking in Infancy

quote.text: Those who walk in infancy are those who let others lead them through life and never learn to think for themselves.
quote.speaker: Jennings

traditional.text: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain because you are slow to learn. In fact, though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you the elementary truths of God’s word all over again. You need milk, not solid food! Anyone who lives on milk, being still an infant, is not acquainted with the teaching about righteousness. But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil

remedy.text: We have so much to explain to you about this, and about God’s healing plan as symbolized in the sanctuary service, but it is hard to explain because you think like children — in concrete terms — and you are slow to learn. In fact, though by this time you ought to be able to clearly explain the true meaning of all the symbolism used, instead, you need someone to teach you the basic truths of God's character all over again! You need to be spoon-fed baby food because you can't handle solid food! Anyone who still lives on the baby food of symbols and metaphors is an infant in their thinking and doesn't have a clue about God's true character and his Remedy for sin. But the solid food of truth is for the mature, who, by constant use, have trained their faculties to distinguish true from false, good from evil, healthy from unhealthy.

scripture.why: The post's picture of sincere believers who still need milk: they have outsourced their discernment and never trained it.

walks.summary: Sincere believers who let a pastor, creed or commentary do their thinking, and live in fear of getting it wrong.
walks.self_check: When I am unsure what is true, do I reason it through from God's design, or do I ask whose authority to defer to?

walks.title: Walking the Line

quote.text: Rule-keepers focus on walking the line, on carefully managing their behavior according to the rules, while failing to understanding and experience God’s transforming love and methods.
quote.speaker: Jennings

walks.summary: Rule-keepers who manage behaviour against a list, judge others by it, and collapse when keeping the rules does not bring the promised blessing.
walks.self_check: When trouble hits after I have 'kept all the rules', is my first thought that God owes me better, or that I never understood how his universe actually works?

walks.title: Walking in Confusion

quote.text: People who walk in confusion are those who cannot differentiate truth from error, who get overwhelmed by the plethora of divergent ideas, and who haven’t understood God’s design laws.
quote.speaker: Jennings

walks.summary: People who cannot tell truth from error amid competing churches and claims, and have no constant to test them against.
walks.self_check: When two teachers disagree, do I have any fixed point, such as how life actually works, to test them by?

walks.title: Walking Alone (wandering away)

quote.text: Those who walk alone have gotten busy with life, or mission, or responsibilities and have slowly wandered away from God.
quote.speaker: Jennings

walks.summary: Mature believers who know God's methods, got busy living them, and slowly stopped spending time with God without noticing.
walks.self_check: When did I last spend unhurried time with God that was not about a task, a sermon or a problem?

walks.title: Walking in Rebellion

quote.text: These are people who have had a knowledge of God but for various reasons have chosen to reject that truth and replace it with some lie
quote.speaker: Jennings

traditional.text: For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened. Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles

remedy.text: For although they knew the truth about God and his methods, they did not appreciate his gracious, humble character nor did they honor him by trusting him and incorporating his methods into their lives. Therefore their reasoning was damaged, their consciences seared, their thoughts became illogical and irrational, and their minds were darkened with lies and falsehoods. They deceived themselves and claimed to be wise, but were actually fools who lost the ability to discern the right from the wrong, the healthy from the unhealthy, the true from the false, and exchanged the values, methods and principles of the immortal God for man-made figurines of mortal humans, birds, mammals and reptiles, and even developed theories that humanity evolved from such lower creatures.

scripture.why: The post's text for knowing God and choosing a lie instead: the rejection is deliberate, and the darkening follows.

traditional.text: They purposely ignore the fact that long ago God gave a command, and the heavens and earth were created

remedy.text: First of all, understand and don't be surprised that in the last days, scoffers and doubters will arise: they will prefer the sickness of selfishness while ridiculing the cure, labeling the infection of selfishness as 'normal.' They will say, "Survival-of-the-fittest is the way the universe runs: this is why we are here — not because of divine creation. Where is this so-called God? Where is the coming he promised? Ever since human history has been recorded, the principles of evolution have governed life, and all things continue just as they always have." But these scoffers deliberately deny the truth and ignore the fact that long ago, by God's Word, the world was created out of water and with water.

scripture.why: The post pairs Peter's scoffers with the rebel: the truth about the Creator is not missing but wilfully ignored.

walks.summary: People who once knew God and have deliberately traded that truth for a lie, and so can never find the peace that only harmony with God gives.
walks.self_check: Is there a truth about God I once held and have set aside because it cost me something?

walks.title: Walking with God

quote.text: This is the goal; this is the way; this is the only path of health and life — to walk with God so closely that this world of selfishness is cut out of our hearts and we are fully united with God, such that we are ready to walk right into heaven!
quote.speaker: Jennings

traditional.text: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him away

remedy.text: Enoch walked with God and then he disappeared from the earth, because God took him away.

scripture.why: Enoch is the post's one-verse picture of the destination: a walk so close that heaven is simply the next step.

walks.summary: Daily, deliberate companionship with God in Scripture, nature and the life of Christ, until selfishness is cut out and we are ready for heaven.
walks.self_check: Is my time with God today a conversation I want, or an item I schedule?

reflection.intro: You have now heard the same act explained seven ways. The point of this page is not to grade anyone else. Jennings turns the levels on the reader ("Your answers will reveal much about the level at which you are currently operating"): listen for which reason sounded most like your own, and notice that God meets people at every level.

guidance.text: Your answers will reveal much about the level at which you are currently operating.
guidance.speaker: Jennings

guidance.text: God, like a loving parent, reaches out to all his children regardless of their level of development. He meets people where they are and throughout human history has spoken to his children in a voice they needed to hear.
guidance.speaker: Jennings

guidance.text: Growth requires exertion; we must think for ourselves.
guidance.speaker: Jennings

guidance.text: Generally, in normal human development, one can only get their mind around one developmental level above the one they are currently operate at.
guidance.speaker: Jennings

guidance.text: Each day, tell God, “Father, I want a heart and mind that is sensitive to truth because all truth leads back to you. Help me see, comprehend, and assimilate your truth at the earliest possible moment that I am capable. Expand my mind to discern ever deeper insights into your kingdom and methods. Change me; take away the longing for selfishness and worldliness and instill your love for life, health, goodness, and people. May it no longer be my fearful self who lives, but may your character of love live in me!”
guidance.speaker: Jennings

prompts: Pick one thing you did today without thinking (brushed your teeth, paid a bill, kept a promise). Write the honest reason you did it, then ask: which of the seven reasons is that?
Think of a rule you keep mainly because of who is watching or what it would cost to break it. What would have to be true for you to keep it with no one watching?
Recall the last time someone broke a rule you value. Was your first feeling that they should be punished, or that they were hurting themselves? What does that reveal?

Jennings says that, generally, we can only get our minds around one level above the one we operate at. Describe, as fairly as you can, how someone one level up from you might explain something you do.
Of the eight roads, which one did you recognise yourself on, and what is one concrete thing you could do this week to walk differently?

poll.question: Which of the seven reasons sounded most like your own reason for doing right today?

glossary.meaning: Rules made up by an authority and enforced by inflicted punishment, the way human governments work; Jennings' name for the mindset of levels one to four.
glossary.quote: Those who follow our ministry know that I consistently contrast the difference between human imposed laws, made-up rules that require inflicted punishments—the legal way of seeing things—with God’s design laws, the protocols the Creator built reality to operate upon, like the laws of health, physics, and the moral laws.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: The protocols the Creator built reality to run on (physics, gravity, health, love, liberty, worship); constants that never change, so they can be used to test any doctrine or idea.
glossary.quote: I teach them to start by developing an understanding of God’s design laws. These are the protocols upon which reality is built to operate. These design laws are constants; they never change — so they are powerful touchstones that we can turn to in order to test the various doctrines, belief systems, or ideas being promoted.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Strength comes by exertion: whatever is exercised grows and whatever is unused withers, which is why moral growth cannot be given, only practised.
glossary.quote: One of these laws is the law of exertion, which simply stated is strength comes by exertion. If you want something to grow stronger, you must exercise it; as everyone knows, if you don't use it, you lose it.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Love can exist only where there is freedom; coerce someone and love is damaged, rebellion instilled and individuality eroded.
glossary.quote: Love only exists in the atmosphere of freedom. Violate freedom — for instance, threaten to kill someone who doesn’t love you — and love will be damaged, rebellion will be instilled, and individuality will be eroded.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: By beholding we are changed: we become like the God we actually worship, so the character we ascribe to God shapes our own.
glossary.quote: One of God's design laws is the law of worship—by beholding we are changed. We actually become like the God we admire and worship. In psychiatry, this is known as modeling.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Atonement read as at-one-ment: the restoration of complete unity between God and his creation, which is how level seven understands the cross.
glossary.quote: Atonement at level seven is understood in its true biblical meaning of at-one-ment—complete unity with God—a universe without any deviation from God and his design of love.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Satisfaction, Ransom, Governmental, Penal Substitution, Moral Influence, Christus Victor/Recapitulation: Jennings lines each up with one level of moral development and says that, through a level-seven lens, the metaphors in all of them radiate the same healing message.
glossary.quote: Imposed law divides, as evidenced by theories one through four above. But true unity, genuine at-one-ment, is achieved when we return to design law.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Being so settled into the truth and love of God, in understanding and experience, that nothing can move you; Jennings equates this with level seven.
glossary.quote: They are sealed of God, which is the state of being so settled into the truth and love of God in both understanding and experience that they cannot be moved. These are individuals operating at level seven.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Force used to limit harm (a parent grabbing a child near the road, a quarantine); it protects but cannot transform, so eventually it lets go.
glossary.quote: I would be remiss if I didn't mention one other type of power—restraining power. Restraining power is that force exercised to restrain, restrict, reduce, impede, slow, and/or obstruct injury, pain, suffering, destruction, and evil.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: A. Graham Maxwell's contrast between obeying a rule on the wall and living from a law written in heart and mind; Jennings reads it as imposed law versus design law.
glossary.quote: In a presentation entitled Legal Problems Among Friends, Graham stated, “Servants are governed by the law on the wall. Friends are governed by the law in their hearts and in their minds” (minute 28:52).
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: Jennings' medical image for believers whose growth stops at level four because they take God's law to be imposed rules like human law.
glossary.quote: Because accepting the infection that God's law is functionally like human law—imposed rules—stops growth at level four. It results in spiritual failure to thrive, failure to grow to the full stature of children of God.
glossary.speaker: Jennings

glossary.meaning: God meets immature people with warnings and even threats because that is what they can hear, but fear is a stage to grow out of, not the goal.
glossary.quote: Yes, God does sometimes use methods designed to insight fear, but fear is for children – God is waiting for us to grow up and come to know Him as He really is.
glossary.speaker: Jennings
